name: Lodha Developers Ltd
title: Lodha Developers Ltd - 543287 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Lodha H1 FY27 PAT rose 63% to INR 2,386 crore on revenue of INR 9,460 crore; management expects to beat FY27 profit guidance of about INR 4,000 crore.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 was reported as the strongest half in company history, with PAT of INR 2,386 crore (up 63%), revenue of INR 9,460 crore (up 30%) and pre-sales of INR 96 billion (up 7%). Q2 had no land sales, so management framed Q2 profitability as underlying development-business earnings. Net debt was about INR 52 billion (about 0.2x equity). Management said the festive season in October was strong and that the company expects to beat its 20% profit growth guidance comfortably, while flagging a 25 bp RBI repo hike in October with limited expected impact on the upper-ticket segment.

financial_highlights.metric: H1 pre-sales as share of FY27 guidance

segments.name: Development business (residential)
segments.commentary: Q2 earnings described as underlying development profitability with no land sales in the quarter. Management expects price growth of about 5-7% p.a. against cost growth of about 4% p.a., adding 100-200 bp margin each year.

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: Bangalore pre-sales exceeded INR 1,800 crore in Q2. Lodha Beaumont Estate (70-acre, North Bangalore) sold about INR 1,500 crore-plus in the first 3 months. FY26 sales were about INR 2,300 crore; FY27 pre-sales are expected above INR 3,000 crore with six operating projects by FY27 end.

segments.name: Data centre platform
segments.commentary: Power availability raised to 5 GW from 3 GW based on approvals; AWS, STT and Digital Edge are building on site. Next land transaction expected in Q4 at about INR 15 billion, with one land deal about every 6 months. First BTS box documents targeted this fiscal, with rental income from FY29.

segments.name: Palava / Extended Eastern suburbs
segments.commentary: Mulund-Airoli-Palava freeway is clinically complete and expected to open within weeks. Management expects significant pre-sales uptick at Palava in CY27, though no specific sales guidance was given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance maintained at about INR 24,000 crore, with H2 development pre-sales of INR 6,000-7,000 crore each in Q3 and Q4 plus a data centre land transaction of about INR 1,500 crore in Q4.
FY27 launch GDV for H2 is just under INR 20,000 crore; FY27 launch guidance was cut to INR 23,100 crore from INR 25,000 crore in July, per the analyst's reading of the slides.
Expects to beat 20% PAT growth guidance (which implied just over INR 4,000 crore) comfortably; no FY28 guidance given yet.
FY27 operating cash flow expected at about INR 85 billion.
DevCo targeted to become net debt-free in 2-3 years.
Data centre target of 1 GW BTS input power signed by FY30 and delivered by FY32; BTS rental of INR 20-23 billion per GW per annum reiterated.
capex_capacity: Construction spend run-rate of about INR 13-13.5 billion per quarter in H1 FY27; management expects a further pickup in H2 as monsoon slowdown eases.
Data centre campus power raised to 5 GW input (a little over 4 GW IT output) from 3 GW; company is funding substation build-out at its own cost.
BTS data centre: definitive documents and construction targeted in FY27 for the first box, with delivery to tenant in FY29.
About 3.9 million sq ft completed unsold inventory, unchanged QoQ; management attributed this to coincidence of delivery timing rather than a stock build-up.
Mumbai Metropolitan Region launch pipeline of about INR 100 billion GDV, of which South-Central Mumbai about INR 40 billion.
First Gurugram NCR project launched in the festive season (commercial office); two more residential pilot projects planned, with a third site possibly added.
demand_pricing: Q2 sales: a little under one-third came from new launches, with the rest from sustenance; H2 mix expected similar or slightly higher launch share.
YTD price growth about 4%; sales mix about 50% in the INR 1-5 crore band (average LTV high-40s to low-50s) and the balance above INR 5 crore.
NRI demand from the Gulf is about 4-5% of sales, mainly entry-level INR 1-3 crore homes; no other meaningful footfall impact from the West Asia situation.
Bangalore market: absorption of about INR 52,500 crore in H1 CY26, up 10% YoY; pricing up about 6% YoY; INR 2 crore-plus segment about 50% of demand.
Management says branded Grade A+/A developers are gaining share and pricing power, while commoditised supply sees less pricing traction.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment has been hit most by the West Asia war, and how is the luxury segment trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Only NRI sales from the Middle East (4-5% of sales, mostly INR 1-3 crore homes) were affected; Central Mumbai luxury demand described as strong.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 launch guidance cut to INR 23,100 crore while pre-sales guidance was held at INR 24,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said launches shift by a month or two routinely and that one project moved from Q4 into Q1 FY28 without changing the pre-sales outlook.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the data centre power upgrade to 5 GW?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase reflects approvals received; the power is available from the existing transmission ecosystem, with the company funding substations. Management estimated $150 billion-plus of potential investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected size and land value of the next data centre transaction?
qa_highlights.answer: A multi-hundred-MW BTS transaction is expected; the land deal is expected at about high-INR 50s crore per acre versus INR 42 crore per acre in the last deal, against an earlier INR 65 crore fair-value estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Are BTS rental assumptions changing?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 20 billion per GW per annum is seen as conservative; guidance of INR 20-23 billion per GW is unchanged for now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin driver behind improved profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Price growth of about 6% against cost growth of about 4% adds 100-200 bp of margin a year, plus supply-chain value extraction; management says this is blended profitability, including new cities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the construction cost impact from the Middle East crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Energy-intensive items such as tiles show inflation, but these are a small share of cost; the company carries a 10% construction cost contingency and 3% project revenue contingency.

risks_watch: Interest rates: 25 bp repo hike in October; INR 1-5 crore segment (about 50% of sales) has mortgage exposure, and entry-level Palava and Extended Eastern suburbs buyers are most sensitive.
Launch slippage: 1-2 H2 launches may move by a month or two, and H2 launch GDV is about INR 20,000 crore, so timing risk is material to the INR 24,000 crore pre-sales target.
Data centre execution: first BTS documents and construction are targeted in FY27 and delivery in FY29; the land deal is expected in Q4 and is a confidential, multi-hundred-MW transaction.
Construction disruption from Maharashtra air-quality rules and water scarcity in the next 3-4 months.
Construction cost inflation in energy-intensive materials as oil prices stay elevated.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on profitability, pre-sales and data centre progress. Management was more guarded on the impact of rate hikes and the Middle East situation, and gave no FY28 guidance and few hard numbers on data centre economics beyond the 1 GW target and rental range.
key_quotes: The first half of fiscal '27 has been the strongest in Lodha's history.
Both the embedded EBITDA as well as the PAT are a real reflection of the strength of profitability of the business, driven by the strength of our brand.
So, just doing this with discipline, price growth around 6%, cost growth around 4%, is adding 100, 150, 200 basis points to margin each year, which really is helpful.

adds.what: Lodha data centre campus power availability raised to 5 GW input from 3 GW (approvals-based, not physical capacity)
First BTS data centre box (1 GW BTS target by FY30, delivery FY32); first box construction targeted FY27, tenant delivery FY29
Mulund-Airoli-Palava freeway expected to open within weeks (infrastructure, not company capacity)

growth.why: Management expects to easily beat the 20% FY27 PAT growth guidance (just over INR 4,000 crore), backed by H1 PAT of INR 2,386 crore (+63%), H1 revenue +30%, and a ~INR 24,000 crore pre-sales guide with H2 pre-sales of INR 6,000-7,000 crore per quarter; however, FY27 launch GDV was cut to INR 23,100 crore from INR 25,000 crore and no FY28 guidance was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects price growth of about 5-7% p.a. against cost growth of about 4% p.a., adding 100-200 bp of margin each year; YTD price growth about 4%, and H1 PAT rose 63% to INR 2,386 crore on revenue up 30%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Data centre power availability raised to 5 GW from 3 GW on approvals, and the first BTS box is targeted for construction in FY27 with tenant delivery in FY29, but physical capacity is not yet live; no residential capacity addition is discussed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H2 development pre-sales guided at INR 6,000-7,000 crore per quarter against FY27 pre-sales guidance of about INR 24,000 crore, with H1 at about 40.3% of guidance; launch GDV is cut to INR 23,100 crore from INR 25,000 crore, so volume risk is material.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Construction spend runs at INR 13-13.5 billion per quarter with a H2 pickup expected, and data centre substation build-out is self-funded; no new residential capex or land plan is stated beyond the Q4 data centre land deal (about INR 1,500 crore) and the INR 100 billion MMR launch pipeline.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects to easily beat the 20% FY27 PAT growth guidance (which implied just over INR 4,000 crore), backed by H1 PAT up 63%; no FY28 guidance given yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Launch GDV cut to INR 23,100 crore from INR 25,000 crore, H2 launch GDV is just under INR 20,000 crore, and 1-2 H2 launches may slip a month or two; rate hike and Maharashtra construction disruption are headwinds.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: H2 launch GDV just under INR 20,000 crore, with MMR pipeline of about INR 100 billion (South-Central Mumbai about INR 40 billion), two more Gurugram residential pilots planned, and Bangalore Beaumont sales above INR 1,500 crore in first 3 months.

rows.label: Data centre land deal and BTS platform
rows.why: At least one land transaction of about INR 15 billion (about INR 1,500 crore) expected in Q4, with one deal about every 6 months, and first BTS box documents targeted this fiscal with rental income from FY29 at INR 20-23 billion per GW per annum.

rows.label: Bangalore pre-sales ramp
rows.why: Bangalore pre-sales exceeded INR 1,800 crore in Q2 and FY27 is expected above INR 3,000 crore, up from about INR 2,300 crore in FY26, with six operating projects by FY27 end.

rows.label: Price growth against cost growth spread
rows.why: Price growth of about 5-7% p.a. against cost growth of about 4% p.a., YTD price growth about 4%, and Bangalore pricing up about 6% YoY, with branded developers gaining pricing power.

tone.note: Management was confident on profit beat, pre-sales and data centre progress, and cautious on rate hikes, Middle East NRI demand and construction cost inflation; analysts pushed on the launch GDV cut and data centre economics.
